## Simple explanation

A sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) model turns one sequence into another. It
can translate a sentence into another language, convert speech into text,
or summarize a document.

## Technical explanation

Seq2seq systems use an encoder to represent the source sequence and a
decoder to generate the target sequence. Attention lets the decoder access
different parts of the source during generation. Architectures include
recurrent encoder-decoders and encoder-decoder Transformers.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Many language and multimodal tasks involve transforming one ordered
representation into another. Seq2seq design handles variable-length inputs
and outputs, but requires careful tokenization, masking, decoding, and
evaluation.

## How it works

The encoder processes source tokens into contextual representations. The
decoder generates target tokens step by step, conditioning on previous
outputs and often attending to the encoder representations. Training commonly
uses teacher forcing; inference uses a decoding strategy such as greedy
decoding or beam search.

The exact architecture varies; many modern implementations use
Transformer encoders and decoders.

## Practical example

For translation, the encoder reads the source sentence and the decoder
generates the translated sentence until it emits an end-of-sequence token.
Evaluation should account for valid alternative translations, not just
exact string matches.

## Common misconceptions

- An encoder-decoder model is not the only way to perform sequence
  generation; decoder-only models can also transform input text.
- During inference, the complete target sequence is not usually available
  in advance; generation is autoregressive in many seq2seq systems.
